btc_volume.caveat: The comparison is a benchmark, not a validation gate. The FAIB stand age and the managed AU age origin are not guaranteed to be the same clock; young plots can show near-zero BTC volume and are reported as unmatched by volume rather than silently clipped.
btc_volume.join_basis: FAIB plot -> BEC + leading species -> managed FEMIC AU stratum (including combined-species strata) -> FEMIC AU site-index class -> managed AU; BTC /TSR volume interpolated at FAIB stand age. This is the same benchmark join as the grade table, not an operational AU assignment.

rsyc.caveat: RSYC is a stand-level remote-sensing yield product. Its volume response is total volume, not merchantable volume, and it has no tree lists, diameter distribution, grade, or residue. This is a coarse sanity check, not a bucking calibration.
rsyc.curve_join: TSA24 centroid -> RSYC tile and ecodistrict; volume curves at ages 20-140
rsyc.next_step: If the plot-level ecodistrict join is sparse, join all TSA24 VRI polygons to RSYC tiles/ecodistricts and compare area-weighted curves rather than using a centroid-only check.
rsyc.plot_join: sample plot coordinates -> RSYC ecodistrict; plot-level volume at stand age
rsyc.tsa_centroid_ecodistrict: Montane Cordillera/Northern Montane Cordillera/Fraser Basin/Nechako Lowland

tipsy.caveat: TIPSY Yield is treated as m3/ha. Grade and residue surfaces are reported separately by the TSA24 grade benchmark; this volume join does not assert grade equivalence. The sort and price profile is a placeholder.

grade_residue_value_inspection.note: The refreshed TSA24 BTC /TSR output now exposes Logs_Grade_D/F/H/I/J/U/X/Y and Residual_Chips/Sawdust/Shavings/Trim/Bark by age. It still has no value, price, or sort columns.

tipsy.join_basis: BEC + leading species -> managed FEMIC AU stratum (including combined-species strata such as SBS_SX+AT) -> FEMIC AU site-index class -> managed source AU in au_table -> TIPSY curve at FAIB stand age.

caveats: Grade and residue values are direct BTC /TSR model output at the AU site index; no nominal-site-index TAF substitution is applied.
Logs_Grade_D and Logs_Grade_F are zero for every TSA24 AU in this run.
Pilot sort codes are not official BC log grades.
TIPSY residual fibre is mill residue, not harvest residue.
Industrial sort comparison is unavailable because the industrial-logs bank was not requested.

grade_share_comparison.note: Pilot sort codes are dimension-only industrial sorts, not BC log grades.  TIPSY Logs_Grade_* values are BTC model output, not field grades; compare grade groups only as a proxy.

tsa24_grades.join_basis: FAIB plot -> BEC + leading species -> managed FEMIC AU stratum (including combined-species strata) -> FEMIC AU site-index class -> managed AU; BTC /TSR curve interpolated at FAIB stand age. Species fallback uses a mean of the same-species managed AU curves and is labelled separately.

residue_comparison.note: BTC Residual_Chips/Sawdust/Shavings/Trim/Bark are mill-processing residues. The pilot taper residue is harvest slash (top/stump/unmerchantable). The two are not equivalent, so no ratio or error metric is computed. Harvest slash is reported separately from the biomass-live AGB bank.

sort_share_comparison.note: The refreshed TSA24 BTC run used log-grades and residual-fibre banks; it did not request industrial-logs, so the industrial sort surface is not comparable in this pass.

value_comparison.note: The pilot uses product-level BC Interior log prices.  No same-basis interior grade price vector is available, so only shares are reported.

vdyp.caveat: VDYP smooth volume units are assumed m3/ha; the curve may represent gross or total volume while VOL_MER is merchantable. The comparison is indicative, not a gate.
vdyp.join_basis: BEC + leading supported species -> managed FEMIC AU stratum (including combined-species strata) -> FEMIC AU site-index class -> VDYP stratum_code + L/M/H. This is the FEMIC AU crosswalk used as a benchmark join, not an operational AU assignment.

bucker_internal_check.note: The reference bucker returns the full stem as residue when no log is feasible; the ledger independently sets residue = taper total - recovered.

assumptions.agb_source: BTC biomass-live bank, Biomass_Live_Above at the matched managed AU and FAIB stand age, ODT/ha. The stand-level value is reported unscaled as agb_odt_ha_unscaled and volume-scaled for the ledger.
assumptions.allocation: No per-tree AGB is invented. The stand-level AGB is applied to the plot on a per-hectare basis and scaled by observed_merchantable_all / BTC_volume so the AGB and the pilot log volume are on the same plot productivity basis. Merchantable log biomass is expanded from sampled trees by PHF_TREE and then by observed all-tree/sampled-tree merchantable volume. The unscaled AGB is retained for sensitivity.
assumptions.basic_density: Species-specific defaults from rules/bc_basic_density.csv (FVS-BC NBEL/FIA table; not a BC-local sample).
assumptions.definition: harvest_residue_odt = AGB_ODT - merchantable_log_biomass_ODT; merchantable_log_biomass_ODT = sum(log_volume_m3 * basic_density_odt_m3)
assumptions.mill_residue_not_used: BTC Residual_Chips/Sawdust/Shavings/Trim/Bark are mill-processing residues and are not harvest slash; they are deliberately excluded.

volume_ratio_screen.note: Plots outside the observed/BTC volume band are kept in the ledger output but excluded from the primary summary because the AU/age join is not mass-balance defensible.

harvest_residue.caveat: AGB is a stand-level model output, not a plot measurement. The difference between AGB-based slash and taper residue is expected: AGB includes bark, branches, and foliage, while the taper ledger only covers top, stump, and unmerchantable stem sections.

psp_volume.note: Primary comparison is paired sampled trees: observed VOL_MER*PHF_TREE versus bucked log volume*PHF_TREE. The *_all columns use all live supported trees in each selected plot on the observed side and a ratio-expanded bucked estimate; that is a secondary estimate.

sample.method: stratified plots by BEC zone and supported leading species; up to max_trees_per_plot trees per plot, sampled across species and DBH
